video_title: Dusty May Postgame Press Conference | Mavericks at Suns | Nov. 27, 2026

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on Mavericks' ability to win without Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving
quotes.excerpt: It gives us confidence and belief. Obviously, we lean on Kai for a lot.
quotes.quote: Even without Cooper's minutes, we were able to hold it down. It gives us confidence and belief. Obviously, we lean on Kai for a lot, and for us to simply stay with it and Max come in, stay ready, and get those minutes that would usually be going to Kai and really take advantage of it. We need to be able to win in numerous ways with different lineups, and so tonight was a step forward where things weren't necessarily going well, and we just stayed with it and then we found our run late.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May says winning without Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving is a step forward for the Mavericks. He praised the team for staying with it and finding a run late despite the stars being out.

structured.context: Head coach Dusty May discusses the team's ability to win despite the absence of Luka Doncic and Kyrie Irving.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on contributions from Naji Marshall and Max Christie
quotes.excerpt: Because Max made a few, they started top blocking him.
quotes.quote: We were struggling breaking down their defense, and because Max made a few, they started top blocking him. And because they had someone else that they weren't able to muck off of, it gave Naji and Cooper a little bit more space. Obviously, the shots, and I thought Max was poised, his finishing in transition was big. He just played well. I thought he defended. They tried to isolate us down the stretch, and other than one great shot by Gillespie, I felt like we defended well on an island.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May credited Max Christie for his poise and transition finishing tonight. He noted that Christie's shooting forced the defense to adjust, which opened up space for Naji Marshall and Cooper Flagg.

structured.context: Dusty May explains how Max Christie's shooting performance created offensive space for his teammates.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on the team's growth during their recent road trip
quotes.excerpt: The NBA game, no lead is ever safe.
quotes.quote: That's what we're learning, that the NBA game, no lead is ever safe. If you can just stay the course, you're always in position to come back if things fall your way a little bit. You can force the opposition to miss a few shots. I thought our zone got them out of rhythm. Even though they had a good plan and made some shots, it seemed like that took them out of their offensive rhythm a little bit, and then we were able to go back and forth and late in the game, our gap activity and individual defense was excellent.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May on the team's defensive growth. He felt the zone defense took the opposition out of their offensive rhythm and praised the team's gap activity and individual defense down the stretch.

structured.context: Dusty May reflects on the team's defensive adjustments and resilience during their recent road trip.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on Cooper Flagg's late-game shot making
quotes.excerpt: It's his big shot making, first and foremost, his late game, last couple minutes.
quotes.quote: It's his big shot making, first and foremost, his late game, last couple minutes, he gets to his spots and makes big shot after big shot. I also thought this wasn't a night where we shot, I guess, probably worse from the three than we typically would for the value of our shots. I think he would have had well over double-digit assists. I thought he made great reads, great decisions, and that's probably the most rewarding part, the night where we're not making shots, our threes aren't going in, we were able to not let that impact our defense and still rebound and find a way.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May on Cooper Flagg: It is his big shot making, first and foremost. He gets to his spots and makes big shot after big shot.

structured.context: Dusty May praises Cooper Flagg for his late-game shot making and playmaking decisions.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on the team's improved possession battle
quotes.excerpt: At the end of the day, if we don't turn it over, it allows you to miss shots.
quotes.quote: We were disappointed at half that we had given up five offensive rebounds, and in the second half, we only gave up three, so that was solid. At the end of the day, if we don't turn it over, and I don't know if it's four, five, six games now where we've managed to control the turnover battle, it allows you to miss shots. It allows you to not be at your best, but I do think, off memory, we were able to get out in the passing lanes late and turn their turnovers into baskets at a time when we were struggling to generate great looks in the half court.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May says controlling the turnover battle has been key for the Mavericks over the last few games. He noted that it allows the team to stay competitive even when they are not shooting the ball well.

structured.context: Dusty May discusses the team's improvement in rebounding and controlling turnovers during the second half.

quotes.speaker: Dusty May
quotes.summary_phrase: Dusty May on offensive spacing and movement improvements
quotes.excerpt: We were much more intentional slipping some screens, putting some pressure on the rim.
quotes.quote: We were able to find some different spacing and our cutting improved. I thought in the first half, even when we got in the paint, we didn't have any second cuts, we didn't have any movement, and we just kind of left our teammates on an island at times. I thought in the second half, we were much more intentional slipping some screens, putting some pressure on the rim. Those are the plays that I just think we weren't, we were letting our inability to make shots in the first half affect how we were playing the game. In the second half, I thought we just, it was almost like the scoreboard was off and we were just playing.
quotes.social_post: Dusty May on the second half turnaround: We were much more intentional slipping some screens and putting pressure on the rim. It was almost like the scoreboard was off and we were just playing.

structured.context: Dusty May explains how the team improved their offensive spacing and movement in the second half.
